items.title: Section: Training Opens — Three Higher Trainings Named

items.zh: 云何為學？謂三勝學。一、增上戒學，二、增上心學，三、增上慧學。云何增上戒學？謂安住具戒等，如前廣說。是名增上戒學。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, in the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the third part of the second yogic process … What is training? It is the three higher trainings: higher discipline, higher mind, and higher wisdom. What is higher discipline? It is abiding endowed with discipline and so on, as extensively explained earlier. This is called higher discipline.

items.title: Higher Mind-Training Opens: The Four Absorptions

items.zh: 云何增上心學？謂離欲惡不善法，有尋、有伺，離生喜樂，入初靜慮具足安住，乃至能入第四靜慮具足安住，是名增上心學。
items.en: What is higher mind-training? It is being free of desire and unwholesome states, accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with the joy and bliss born of seclusion, entering and fully abiding in the first absorption — up through entering and fully abiding in the fourth absorption. This is called higher mind-training.

items.title: The Formless Attainments; Higher Wisdom Opens

items.zh: 又諸無色，及餘所有等持、等至，亦皆名為增上心學。然依靜慮，能最初入聖諦現觀，正性離生，非全遠離一切靜慮能成此事。是故靜慮最為殊勝，故偏說為增上心學。云何增上慧學？謂於四聖諦等所有如實智見。是名增上慧學。
items.en: The formless attainments, and all other forms of meditative composure and attainment as well, are likewise called higher mind-training. Yet it is specifically in dependence on the four absorptions that one first enters direct insight into the noble truths, entering the true nature that departs from arising — this cannot be accomplished by relying entirely on states apart from the four absorptions. It is for this reason that the absorptions are the most excellent, and higher mind-training is spoken of with particular reference to them. What is higher wisdom-training? It is the as-it-really-is knowledge and vision regarding the four noble truths and so on. This is called higher wisdom-training.

items.title: Why Exactly Three Trainings, No More and No Fewer

items.zh: 問：何緣唯有三學，非少非多？答：建立定義故，智所依義故，辨所作義故。建立定義者，謂增上戒學。所以者何？由戒建立心一境性，能令其心觸三摩地。智所依義者，謂增上心學。所以者何？由正定心念一境性，於所知事有如實智、如實見轉。辨所作義者，謂增上慧學。
items.en: Question: Why are there exactly three trainings, no fewer and no more? Answer: because of establishing concentration, because of serving as wisdom's basis, and because of accomplishing what is to be done. Establishing concentration refers to higher discipline. Why? Because discipline establishes one-pointedness of mind, enabling the mind to touch true concentration. Serving as wisdom's basis refers to higher mind-training. Why? Because through a rightly concentrated mind with one-pointed mindfulness, as-it-really-is knowledge and as-it-really-is vision arise regarding what is to be known. Accomplishing what is to be done refers to higher wisdom-training.

items.zh: 所以者何？由善清淨若智、若見，能證究竟諸煩惱斷。以煩惱斷是自義利，是勝所作，過此更無勝所作故。由是因緣，唯有三學。問：何緣三學如是次第？

items.title: Section: The Twelve-Link Chain from Pure Discipline to Final Nirvana

items.zh: 答：先於尸羅善清淨故，便無憂悔；無憂悔故，歡喜安樂；由有樂故，心得正定；心得定故，能如實知、能如實見；如實知見，故能起厭；厭故離染；由離染故，便得解脫；得解脫故，證無所作究竟涅槃。
items.en: Answer: First, through discipline well purified, there is no anxiety or regret. Through no anxiety or regret, there is gladness and ease. Through this ease, the mind attains right concentration. Through a concentrated mind, one is able to know and see as things really are. Through this true knowing and seeing, revulsion arises. Through revulsion, dispassion follows. Through dispassion, liberation is attained. Through liberation, one realises final nirvana, in which nothing further remains to be done.

items.zh: 如是最初修習淨戒，漸次進趣，後證無作究竟涅槃。是故三學如是次第。問：何緣三學名為增上戒、心、慧耶？答：所趣義故，最勝義故，名為增上。云何所趣義？謂為趣增上心而修淨戒，名增上戒學。為趣增上慧而修定心，名增上心學。為趣煩惱斷而修智見，名增上慧學。如是名為所趣義故，名為增上。云何最勝義？謂若增上戒學、若增上心學、若增上慧學，唯於聖教獨有此三，不共外道。如是名為最勝義故，名為增上。又或有增上心學能引發增上慧學，或有增上慧學能引發增上心學。謂聖弟子未得根本靜慮，先學見跡，後為進斷修道所斷一切煩惱，正勤加行，修念覺支，乃至修捨覺支，是名增上慧學引發增上心學。增上心學引發增上慧學者，如前已說。

items.title: Partial Trainings, and Three Practitioners by Degree of Detachment

items.zh: 又或有增上戒學，無增上心、無增上慧；或有增上戒學，亦有增上心，唯無增上慧；非有增上慧學，而無增上戒及無增上心。是故若有增上慧學，當知必定具足三學。於此建立三種學中，諸瑜伽師當勤修學。復有三種補特伽羅，依此三學入諦現觀。何等為三？一、未離欲，二、倍離欲，三、已離欲。當知此中，於一切欲全未離者，勤修加行，入諦現觀；既於諸諦得現觀已，證預流果。倍離欲者，當於爾時證一來果。已離欲者，當於爾時證不還果。
items.en: A practitioner may have higher discipline alone, without higher mind or higher wisdom; or may have both higher discipline and higher mind, but lack higher wisdom alone; but there is no case of having higher wisdom while lacking higher discipline and higher mind. Therefore, wherever higher wisdom is present, the other two trainings are necessarily present as well. There are, further, three kinds of practitioner who enter direct insight into the truths by means of these three trainings: one not yet detached from desire, one doubly detached from desire, and one fully detached from desire. One entirely not yet detached from desire … realises the fruit of stream-entry. One doubly detached from desire, at that same point, realises the fruit of once-returning. One fully detached from desire, at that same point, realises the fruit of non-returning.

items.title: The Three Faculties: Not-Yet-Knowing, Already-Knowing, Fully-Knowing

items.zh: 復有三根。一、未知欲知根，二、已知根，三、具知根。云何建立如是三根？謂於諸諦未現觀者，加行勤修諸諦現觀，依此建立未知欲知根。若於諸諦已得現觀，而居有學，依此建立已知根。若阿羅漢所作已辦，住無學位，依此建立具知根。
items.en: There are, further, three faculties: the faculty of wishing to know what is not yet known; the faculty of having already known; and the faculty of complete knowing. Regarding one who has not yet attained direct insight into the truths, diligently applying effort towards that insight — on this basis the faculty of wishing to know what is not yet known is established. Regarding one who has already attained direct insight into the truths but still remains a trainee — on this basis the faculty of having already known is established. Regarding an arhat who has accomplished all that is to be accomplished, abiding beyond training — on this basis the faculty of complete knowing is established.

blocks.text: Fascicle 28 answers several of the seventeen questions: training, what supports and obstructs it, how yoga can fail, what yoga is, attention, and the cultivation of the factors of awakening, including the four foundations of mindfulness. A passage at 0436a22 is untranslated.

"Training is the three higher trainings: higher discipline, higher mind, higher wisdom." Higher mind is the four absorptions; "it is specifically in dependence on the four absorptions that one first enters direct insight into the noble truths". Higher wisdom is "the as-it-really-is knowledge and vision regarding the four truths".
"Because of establishing concentration, serving as wisdom's basis, and accomplishing what is to be done."

"Through discipline well purified, there is no anxiety or regret; through that, gladness and ease; through ease, right concentration; through concentration, true knowing and seeing; then disenchantment, dispassion, liberation", up to nirvāṇa with nothing more to be done. (Compare Day 190.)

The untranslated prose (0436a22) explains "higher" (增上) in two senses: **leading towards** (discipline leads to concentration, concentration to wisdom, wisdom to the end of afflictions) and **supreme** (found only in the Buddha's teaching). It adds that concentration and wisdom can each draw the other forth: a disciple who sees the truths before attaining the absorptions develops the factors of awakening, and so wisdom leads to concentration.
One may have discipline without the other two, or discipline and mind without wisdom; "but wherever higher wisdom is present, the other two are necessarily present".
The faculty of "wishing to know what is not yet known" (the path of seeing), "having already known" (the trainee), and "complete knowing" (the arhat).

quiz.q: Which of the seventeen sections does Master Cháng Bǎi say this fascicle covers?
options: from the fifth, training, to the twelfth, cultivation of yoga, which continues into fascicle 29
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this fascicle covers the fifth of seventeen sections, "training," through the twelfth, "cultivation of yogic practice," which continues into fascicle 29.

quiz.q: The formless attainments are also higher mind; why single out the four absorptions, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say of the fourth?
options: by the absorptions one first enters insight into the truths; the fourth balances concentration and wisdom — the Buddha awakened there
quiz.why: "It is specifically in dependence on the four absorptions that one first enters direct insight into the noble truths … It is for this reason that the absorptions are the most excellent." Master Cháng Bǎi: for cultivating the path, the fourth absorption is where concentration and wisdom are balanced, so the Buddha attained supreme awakening in it.

quiz.q: Why are there exactly three trainings, no fewer and no more?
options: establishing concentration, being wisdom's basis, accomplishing the task: discipline establishes concentration, concentration supports wisdom, wisdom completes the work
quiz.why: "Because of establishing concentration, because of serving as wisdom's basis, and because of accomplishing what is to be done." Master Cháng Bǎi: discipline establishes concentration, concentration is wisdom's basis, wisdom accomplishes the task — so these three are set up.

quiz.q: Where does the sequence of the three trainings begin, and what two kinds of precept-holders does Master Cháng Bǎi name?
options: first, through pure discipline, no regret; one kind has never broken precepts since ordination — pure from the start
quiz.why: "First, through discipline well purified, there is no anxiety or regret." Master Cháng Bǎi: those who keep pure discipline are of two kinds; one has never broken a precept since ordination — pure from the beginning.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "nothing further to be done"?
options: beyond this there is nothing more excellent to do — the arhat beyond training
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beyond this stage there is nothing more excellent to be done — that is "nothing to be done," the arhat beyond training.

quiz.q: Does one with higher wisdom necessarily have all three, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say of discipline and concentration?
options: wherever higher wisdom is, all three are present; concentration always includes discipline, but discipline need not include concentration or wisdom
quiz.why: "Therefore, wherever higher wisdom is present, the other two trainings are necessarily present as well." Master Cháng Bǎi: concentration necessarily includes discipline, but discipline does not necessarily include concentration or wisdom.

quiz.q: What are the three faculties, and how many faculties does Venerable Miào Jìng say make up "wishing to know" for one at the stages of warmth through highest worldly dharma?
options: wishing to know, having known, complete knowing; at those stages, ten faculties belong to "wishing to know"
quiz.why: "The faculty of wishing to know what is not yet known; the faculty of having already known; and the faculty of complete knowing." Venerable Miào Jìng: for the practitioner at warmth, summit, patience, and highest worldly dharma, ten faculties all belong to "wishing to know."
